topic: Cost-optimal physical acquisition certificates for counterfactual identification. For a finite discrete ADMG G with explicit physical action expansion G+, domains of size at most d, and a priced catalogue of SELECT/RAND/CTF-RAND/READ actions with endpoints, affected child sets, allowed values, precedence, and conflicts, optimize total acquisition cost over legal protocol/slice collections making the full, correctly typed unconditional CTFIDU+ procedure accept an unnested L2.5 joint Q. A protocol is a subset bit-vector in canonical topological order with exactly one fresh-iid SELECT and each mechanism used at most once. Action costs are nonnegative binary rationals paid anew per distinct acquired protocol; slices from that protocol share its cost. Output one optimal protocol collection, polynomial assignment labels, and for each of k structural target factors a chosen input regime and finite uniform value-matching ancestor/district restriction transcript. Prove the <=k source-slice sparsification, fixed-factor connected-ancestor obstruction iff theorem, and cost-preserving legality/obstruction compilation on V⊔A⊔LIT⊔FAC with Dir/Bidir/Source/Affects/Precedes/Conflicts/Owns/HasValue/InFactor/RequestedBy, yielding exact f(k,d,w)poly(input) optimization for full Gaifman incidence treewidth w. Retain ordinary legal-subclass hardness and H_k approximation only on the explicit one-action/no-synergy factor-cover subclass. Preserve positive-law and measured-ancestry source typing. No scalar identifying-functional output, evaluation, or compactness theorem is claimed; general lower certificates may be exponential. Do not claim conditional or arbitrary partial-read completeness, mediator-depth FPT, or global action-cover approximation. Consumer: Park-Lee counterfactual structural causal bandits (ICLR 2026), whose reward-distribution queries can use cheaper certified acquisition protocols. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For a fixed labelled source factor T and target C, IDENTIFY+ fails exactly when some C⊊F⊆T is bidirected connected and every vertex of F reaches C in its value-matching dependency graph. The obstruction survives each ancestor and district restriction; terminal failure supplies a witness. Independent exhaustive checks through four vertices covered 28,751 cases with zero mismatches. Two binary SCMs agree under all 27 ordinary intervention regimes but differ on P(Y_0=1,Z_1=1). Independent response noise ε=0.1 preserves positive laws and yields 1/4 versus 41/100. A cost-1 counterfactual protocol identifies the joint from its natural-X=1 slice, compared with the direct cost-2 protocol. The output contract avoids the exponential scalar-functional objection; positivity and measured ancestral closure remain explicit source-typing requirements. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove full CTFIDU+ acceptance equivalent to at most k uniform source-slice certificates and a cost-preserving local relational compilation whose width includes every action, conflict, precedence, and value request. EARLY KILL TEST: Exhaustively compare full acceptance and uniform certificates on binary instances with at most four mechanism vertices, four intervention actions, and two factors, including equal-value cases and omitted READs; unrecorded assignment-dependent switching or more than k required slices forces a pivot. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_ctf_protocol_cost_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For a finite discrete ADMG, an unnested L2.5 joint query, and a priced catalogue of legal SELECT/RAND/CTF-RAND/READ actions, characterize and compute the minimum-cost collection of physical protocols whose induced source slices makes unconditional CTFIDU+ accept the query.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves CTFIDU+ complete for identification from arbitrary Layer-3 distributions, but does not optimize which physically acquired inputs or slices should be purchased.
source_refs.author: Arvind Raghavan and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: The paper completely characterizes which counterfactual distributions can be sampled by physically feasible operations, but does not optimize reusable collections of such operations for identifying another query.
source_refs.author: Arvind Raghavan and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: The paper optimizes permitted interventions for identifying an L2 causal effect and proves NP-hardness plus exact and logarithmic-approximation results, but does not cover L3 inputs or physical counterfactual protocols.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, and Negar Kiyavash

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest literature separates three layers that the proposed result must couple: CTFIDU+ takes an arbitrary source collection as fixed, counterfactual realizability decides whether an individual counterfactual law can be sampled physically, and minimum-cost intervention design optimizes ordinary L2 experiments. None represents protocol-level precedence, conflicts, allowed values, READ projections, or a cost paid once for several slices. The first proof step that changes from ordinary intervention design is the obstruction-cover reduction: L2 hedges are replaced by typed L2.5 factors whose admissible sources depend on uniform value-matching restrictions and shared protocol ownership.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sound-and-complete minimum-cost certificate theorem returning an optimal legal protocol collection and factor-to-source restriction transcripts, together with a precisely scoped hardness and approximation frontier.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from newly available Layer-3 data to complete counterfactual identification, then make economical selection of those inputs the new destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Physically realizable counterfactual data enlarges the available source class -> CTFIDU+ characterizes identification from a fixed arbitrary source collection -> several physical collections may certify the same query -> choose the cheapest legal collection.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over CTFIDU+'s counterfactual factorization, typed source reductions, and completeness argument, while exposing each accepted source use as a finite certificate transcript.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired optimization predicate is exactly acceptance by this algorithm, augmented with physical source typing and reusable protocol ownership.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the graphical-obstruction hitting-set formulation, weighted hardness reduction, exact solver, and harmonic approximation proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest query-specific acquisition-cost result, while the new obstruction family and cost sharing arise from counterfactual factors and physical protocols.

method_exemplars.technique: After certificate selection, construct source-aligned influence functions and asymptotically linear estimators by projecting factor contributions into the tangent spaces of their acquired slices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A certificate aligns different parts of the target law with multiple acquired sources, matching the structural setting of efficient estimation under data fusion.

open_problems.open_problem: Does acceptance of an unnested finite-discrete counterfactual joint from physically typed source slices admit a normal form using at most one uniformly chosen source slice per target factor, with a finite value-matching ancestor/district restriction transcript?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves complete identification from arbitrary Layer-3 inputs through CTFIDU+, but does not state a protocol-slice sparsification or uniform-source normal form.
source_refs.author: Arvind Raghavan and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: ctfID reduces counterfactual queries to factors and tests each against fixed observational and experimental inputs, without projected READ slices or reusable protocol ownership.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa, Sanghack Lee, and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: The paper shows generalized identification requires explicit positivity and replaces an unsound earlier argument with a positivity-aware decomposition into classical identification subproblems.
source_refs.author: Yaroslav Kivva, Ehsan Mokhtarian, Jalal Etesami, and Negar Kiyavash

open_problems.why_unsolved: Factorization suggests one input witness per target district, but existing completeness theorems quantify over already available distributions and do not normalize successful runs involving projected READ slices, measured-ancestry typing, and several slices owned by one paid protocol. A proof must rule out assignment-dependent switching among sources and show that each recursive run can be replaced by a uniform source choice for every factor. Positivity is load-bearing because generalized-identification arguments are known to become unsound when restriction steps silently use unsupported events.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An iff theorem converting every successful correctly typed unconditional CTFIDU+ run into at most k uniform factor-source transcripts and converting terminal failure into a fixed-factor connected-ancestor obstruction, or a finite counterexample disproving that normal form.

writing_exemplar.why: Its complete-algorithm narrative supplies the exact proof boundary at which a bounded, physically typed certificate normal form must be established.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Layer-3 inputs permit additional counterfactual identification -> CTFIDU+ gives a complete recursive acceptance procedure -> cost optimization requires finite local witnesses rather than opaque runs -> normalize every accepting run to one uniform slice transcript per target factor.

method_exemplars.technique: Strengthen the algorithm's ancestor and district restriction induction so its existential source-selection steps emit uniform factor-level witnesses and its terminal failures emit fixed-factor obstructions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested transcript follows the same recursive restrictions as CTFIDU+ and must preserve its soundness and completeness.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse counterfactual unnesting, ancestral-set reduction, c-component factorization, and the countermodel argument associated with failed factor identification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the structurally analogous factor-level proof moves that the physical-source normal form must refine.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the positivity-aware decomposition and completeness proof to ensure every restriction transcript preserves support and source compatibility.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Typed projected sources create the same risk of treating unsupported or incompatible input laws as interchangeable.

open_problems.open_problem: Is minimum-cost legal counterfactual-certificate selection fixed-parameter tractable in the number of target factors k, maximum domain size d, and treewidth w of the full action-literal-factor incidence structure?

source_refs.claim: Minimum-cost L2 intervention design is NP-hard in general, with polynomial algorithms supplied for restrictive structures such as tree-shaped directed and bidirected subgraphs.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, and Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: MSO-definable weighted evaluations can be computed recursively on bounded-treewidth graph decompositions using semiring homomorphisms.
source_refs.author: Bruno Courcelle and Mohamed Mosbah

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes efficient algorithms for broad logically definable optimization problems on graphs of fixed bounded treewidth.
source_refs.author: Stefan Arnborg, Jens Lagergren, and Detlef Seese

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing causal-design tractability uses restrictive geometry of the directed and bidirected causal graph, whereas a physical protocol instance also contains actions, values, source slices, ownership, affected-child relations, conflicts, precedence, and factor requests. Bounded causal-graph treewidth does not control those cross-cutting constraints. A Courcelle-style transfer first requires a cost-preserving finite relational encoding in which legality and each factor obstruction are MSO-definable and whose Gaifman width includes every catalogue relation; the causal-design literature supplies no such compilation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit relational compilation and weighted-MSO or tree-decomposition dynamic program returning an optimal certificate in f(k,d,w)poly(input) time, plus counterexamples showing why omitting action, conflict, precedence, or value-request incidence from w invalidates the result.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its movement from query-specific causal identification to combinatorial cost optimization and then to general hardness versus tractable structural subclasses.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Identifying a causal target may require costly experiments -> query-specific minimum-cost design is NP-hard -> restrictive graph structure restores tractability -> seek parameterized tractability governed by the full physical-protocol incidence structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode certificate feasibility with free set variables in monadic second-order logic and evaluate minimum rational cost over a tree decomposition using a semiring-homomorphism dynamic program.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested result is a weighted logical optimization over a bounded-width relational incidence graph.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply extended-MSO optimization on bounded-treewidth structures, with formula size parameterized by k and d and additive weights attached to selected protocol objects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the canonical bridge from a finite logical certificate predicate to an FPT optimization theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Preserve the query-specific obstruction-cover semantics and ordinary-subclass hardness gadgets while replacing special tree algorithms with a full-incidence treewidth compilation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the appropriate causal optimization semantics and unrestricted hardness baseline.

open_problems.open_problem: Under a budget insufficient for exact identification, which legal physical protocol collection minimizes the sharp identified-set width of a specified finite-discrete L3 query?

source_refs.claim: The paper derives counterfactual bounds using realizable Layer-3 data, but does not optimize a priced choice among physical source collections.
source_refs.author: Arvind Raghavan and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: The paper computes optimal bounds for counterfactual queries from a fixed collection of observational and experimental distributions through canonical finite SCMs and polynomial programs.
source_refs.author: Junzhe Zhang, Jin Tian, and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: The paper optimizes acquisition only for crossing an exact L2-identification threshold, not for tightening an L3 identified set under a fixed budget.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, and Negar Kiyavash

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing partial-counterfactual methods optimize bounds after the source distributions are fixed, while cost-aware causal design optimizes acquisition only for the binary event of exact L2 identification. Choosing a physical protocol changes the equality constraints of the canonical-SCM polynomial program, so identified-set width need not be a static cover objective and may exhibit complementarity among slices from different protocols. No scanned source couples sharp L3 bounds, physical source legality, and budgeted acquisition selection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp characterization or exact optimization theorem for the minimum attainable lower-upper endpoint gap under budget B, with a complexity or approximation boundary and a valid estimator and confidence region for the selected endpoints.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames bounds as the response when even realizable Layer-3 data cannot point-identify the target; the new step makes acquisition choice endogenous.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Realizable counterfactual data enlarges exact identification -> some important targets remain unidentified -> Layer-3 inputs can nevertheless tighten their bounds -> choose the affordable physical inputs that yield the sharpest region.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the canonical finite-SCM response-function parameterization and sharp endpoint polynomial programs, activating equality constraints according to the selected protocol slices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the sharp L3 identified set whose width becomes the acquisition objective.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt weighted experiment selection and its hardness reductions, replacing the exact-identification predicate with a sharp-bound-width threshold oracle.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest cost-aware causal acquisition framework, but its binary objective must become quantitative.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt cross-fitted semiparametrically efficient endpoint estimators, influence-function expansions, and simultaneous confidence-region arguments for partially identified data-fusion targets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Selected protocol slices form multiple data sources, and the resolution requires inference for bound endpoints rather than population sharpness alone.

open_problems.open_problem: For counterfactual structural causal bandits with heterogeneous acquisition costs, can an agent pay once for a certified protocol and reuse its slices to identify several arm reward laws while attaining a regret-plus-acquisition-cost bound against the optimal adaptive acquisition policy?

source_refs.claim: CTF-SCB enlarges the arm space to physically realizable counterfactual actions, but does not model reusable protocol-acquisition costs or indirect identification of several arm laws from shared slices.
source_refs.author: Min Woo Park and Sanghack Lee

source_refs.claim: The paper fuses observational, experimental, and counterfactual information in a Thompson-sampling learner, but assumes rather than optimizes the available data sources.
source_refs.author: Andrew Forney, Judea Pearl, and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: The paper derives efficiency gains and efficient estimators when multiple sources align with different parts of a target law, but source acquisition is not a sequential causal-bandit decision.
source_refs.author: Sijia Li and Alex Luedtke

open_problems.why_unsolved: Park-Lee treats realizable counterfactual actions as arms whose rewards are sampled through physical operations, whereas a cost-optimal certificate may acquire another protocol whose slices identify several arm distributions simultaneously. This creates persistent side information, fixed acquisition charges, and correlated uncertainty across identified arms. The first changed proof step is the armwise concentration argument after graph-based pruning: confidence sets must propagate slice-estimation error through factorized identification maps while the policy decides whether another reusable protocol merits its one-time cost.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An online acquisition-and-play algorithm with finite-time upper and matching lower bounds for cumulative reward regret plus protocol costs, parameterized by the cheapest certificates and statistical information supplied by reusable slices.

writing_exemplar.why: Adopt its expansion and graph-based pruning of counterfactual arms, then expose reusable acquisition as the missing sequential decision layer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Ordinary causal bandits use observational or interventional arms -> physically realizable counterfactual actions enlarge the attainable reward set -> graph structure prunes that enlarged arm space -> acquire shared protocol slices that cheaply certify several surviving reward laws.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the physical-operation realizability criterion to restrict acquisition actions and prove that each acquired source law corresponds to an executable protocol.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every online acquisition must be physically valid independently of the unknown SCM parameters.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt counterfactual data fusion inside Thompson sampling, replacing its fixed source menu with posterior or confidence updates driven by purchased protocol slices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already transfers heterogeneous causal information into bandit decisions; the new theorem must add endogenous reusable acquisition and a cost-sensitive benchmark.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct source-aware asymptotically linear estimators and variance estimates for reward laws identified through several shared slices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The feedback after certificate acquisition is an aligned multi-source problem rather than an independent sample stream for every arm.

literature_map:
Shpitser and Pearl (2008, JMLR) provide foundational complete identification theory for interventional and counterfactual queries.
Bareinboim and Pearl (2012, UAI; arXiv:1210.4842) characterize z-identifiability when experiments are available on a designated surrogate set.
Lee, Correa, and Bareinboim (2020, UAI/PMLR 115) extend generalized identification to arbitrary observational and experimental source collections.
Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2022, UAI; arXiv:2206.01081) expose the positivity defect in earlier gID formulations and give a sound-and-complete repair.
Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (2021, NeurIPS; arXiv:2107.03190) supply counterfactual unnesting, factorization, and complete identification from fixed observational and experimental sources.
Raghavan and Bareinboim (2025, ICLR; arXiv:2503.11870) distinguish identification from realizability and characterize physically sampleable counterfactual distributions.
Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026; arXiv:2602.23541) introduce complete CTFIDU+ identification from arbitrary Layer-3 inputs and derive bounds using realizable counterfactual data.
The 2025 realizability and 2026 CTFIDU+ papers leave acquisition selection exogenous: neither prices reusable physical protocols or compiles acceptance into bounded local certificates.
Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2022, ICML; arXiv:2205.02232) formulate minimum-cost L2 intervention design, prove NP-hardness, and connect it to hitting set.
Kandasamy, Bhattacharyya, and Honavar (2019, AAAI) optimize intervention covers sufficient for all identifiable effects, rather than a typed L2.5 target.
Kocaoglu, Dimakis, and Vishwanath (2017, ICML) and Lindgren et al. (2018, NeurIPS; arXiv:1810.11867) optimize experiments for structure learning rather than counterfactual-query identification.
Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022, ICML; arXiv:2110.05690) compute sharp L3 bounds from fixed sources through canonical finite SCMs and polynomial programming.
Courcelle and Mosbah (1993) and Arnborg, Lagergren, and Seese (1991) provide bounded-treewidth logical optimization machinery, but not the required causal legality and obstruction encoding.
Li and Luedtke (2023, Biometrika; arXiv:2111.14945) provide efficiency theory for aligned multi-source fusion; Jiang and Janson (2025; arXiv:2502.05319) give DML inference for partial-fusion endpoints.
Forney, Pearl, and Bareinboim (2017, ICML) fuse heterogeneous causal information online, while Park and Lee (2026, ICLR) introduce counterfactual structural causal bandits without priced reusable identification certificates.
